title: Structured logging in a travel booking handler
name: Booking request logger

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code attaches per-request context to log records? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A booking fails with a supplier Error and the call site passes { durationMs }. Which fields does the emitted error record contain besides ts, level and msg?
choices: Only durationMs; error details are dropped because fields replaces errFields
error.type, error.message, error.stack, durationMs, plus the logger's bindings
error.message as a stringified object, durationMs, and no bindings
The raw Error object under an "err" key, which JSON.stringify serializes as {}

questions.prompt: A caller passes a field named "level" in fields when calling log.info("booking.started", { level: "vip" }). What appears in the JSON record?
choices: "level": "info", because the logger's own fields are written last
Both values, as level and level_1
"level": "vip", because caller fields are spread after the built-in keys
The record is dropped because "vip" is not a valid level

questions.prompt: LOG_LEVEL is unset in production. Which booking events are written?
choices: None; minLevel is undefined so every comparison is false
All events including debug, since there is no level configured
